title: Aggregate
description:
The window and identity of an aggregate figure. Carried by every event in the `analytical` class and by the aggregate events in `audit`.

The window is a bucket identifier, not a start and end pair. Two buckets either denote the same period or disjoint periods; overlap is unrepresentable rather than merely discouraged. This matters because a k-anonymity floor protects each published figure and does nothing about the arithmetic between them: aggregates over 14:00-15:00 and 14:00-14:30, both above the floor, subtract to a 14:30-15:00 bucket that may hold one person. A schema that let an author choose the endpoints would be a differencing oracle with a floor bolted on.

A corrected figure is republished with the same `aggregate_id` and a higher `revision`. The earlier figure is not withdrawn: both remaining visible is the price of not offering the same differencing channel through revision history. Consumers take the highest revision for an `aggregate_id`.

Buckets below the k-floor are suppressed entirely. A suppressed bucket and an empty bucket are indistinguishable, which means absence - never a zero, a null, or a marker field. There is deliberately nowhere in this type to record that suppression occurred.

aggregate_id.description: Deterministic over the aggregate type, its key dimensions, and its window. Stable across corrections, which is what makes supersession by revision work.

window.description: Bucket identifier. The hour form "2026-09-07T14Z" for a PT1H aggregate, the day form "2026-09-07Z" for a P1D aggregate. MUST match the duration declared in the schema's `x-beb-aggregate.window`, which `beb-lint` checks.

revision.description: 0 for the original figure, incrementing for each correction. Consumers take the highest revision seen for an `aggregate_id`.
